ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, and Apple-IAP / Google-Play payment intermediaries against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, PCMLTFA Schedules 1-2, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, and the OFAC SDN List (best-practice U.S. clearance). Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier requires enhanced due diligence (EDD), source-of-funds verification for contributions above CAD 10,000, ongoing name-match monitoring, and annual re-screening throughout the life of the partnership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) NUANS Federal Name Search; limited partnership declaration filed through the applicable provincial registry (e.g., Ontario Business Registry on a jurisdiction-matched portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Official Languages Act requires corporate and partnership names in English, French, or both. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into English or French. A federal name used across Canada must be bilingual and distinguishable from all existing federal and provincial names under NUANS policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS-based name reservation cannot be extended; a new search and reservation must be filed after the 90-day expiry. Upon rejection, obtain the registrar's written reasons, cure distinctiveness or sensitive-token objections, and resubmit a new NUANS application. For a contested refusal, file a written administrative reconsideration with the Director under CBCA s. 12 (or the corresponding provincial LP director) within 30 days of the refusal, attaching revised evidence of non-confusion and any regulatory consent issued for the sensitive token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where the provider maintains a physical street address within the registration jurisdiction, a dedicated local agent accepting service of process, and mail-forwarding infrastructure. A post-office box or purely virtual address is non-compliant. Acceptable for pre-incorporation, but commercial substance policies for Canadian digital gaming risk oversight may require local personnel and financial records if FINTRAC re-characterizes app-store settlement flows.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium: approximately 10% per annum risk of unannounced provincial registry address-verification site visits; approximately 25-30% per annum risk if FINTRAC classifies the entity as a money services business due to in-app payment aggregation or virtual-currency wallet balances.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, as amended; sections 1-14 (formation, declaration, and registration). Extra-provincial registration under the Ontario Extra-Provincial Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. E.23, where applicable. Federal tax registration under the Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Suppl.), s. 102.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Government of Ontario
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement for limited partnerships; capital contributions are governed by the partnership agreement. No escrow account rule applies unless the partnership issues securities requiring a prospectus or reliance on an exemption.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the formation of the Partnership as a limited partnership registered under Ontario law is hereby ratified; that the initial capital contribution of the General Partner and each Limited Partner is accepted, with subscription schedules attached; that the registered office be established at the address set forth in the Partnership Agreement and that the designated registered agent is appointed; that the General Partner is authorized to maintain the governing books and records; and that the Chief Executive Officer, Treasurer, and Corporate Secretary are appointed to serve until successors are elected; and that the General Partner shall execute all necessary documents, open bank accounts, and engage any professional advisers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR) — online at www.ontariobusinessregistry.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Initiate a NUANS-designated name search and submit a name reservation application through the OBR portal. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee and record the 90-day reservation number. The reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed for one further 90-day period.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion with an existing name, use the NUANS report to select a distinguishing element and file a new reservation. A request for reconsideration may be made to the Director of Companies and Personal Property Security Branch within 30 days of the rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / notarial services (registered Ontario law firm)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft, review, and execute the limited partnership agreement. The agreement must identify all general and limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and rights of limited partners. All partners must execute the agreement before filing. Electronic signatures are permitted under the Electronic Commerce Act, 2000.
required_dossiers: Signed subscription pages from all partners
Power of attorney for any non-resident partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner's signature is incomplete, return the agreement for rectification. A solicitor's certificate may be provided to confirm capacity and execution where any signature is challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 (Declaration of Limited Partnership) to the OBR with the required registration fee. The declaration must state the general partner's legal name, address for service, principal place of business, and confirmation that the partnership is not a personal property security debtor. File via the OBR online portal or at a ServiceOntario centre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the declaration with a deficiency, correct the specified fields and resubmit within 30 days. If the declaration is rejected on jurisdictional grounds, obtain a court order or file in an alternative provincial registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Registrations and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/taxes/business-registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the CRA Business Registration Online portal and supply the limited partnership's legal name, provincial declaration number, and general partner's identification. The system will issue a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and, where the partnership makes taxable sales, a GST/HST account. A payroll account is required if the partnership employs staff.
required_dossiers: General partner's Social Insurance Number or Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA request fails or requires validation, upload the missing declaration and BN confirmation within 10 business days. A request for reconsideration may be filed under section 32 of the Excise Tax Act if the GST/HST account is incorrectly assigned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial corporate registries in each province of extra-provincial operations (e.g., Alberta Corporate Registry, British Columbia Registrar of Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each province where the limited partnership intends to carry on business, file a certified copy of the Ontario Declaration of Limited Partnership and an extra-provincial registration application. Attach a statement appointing a local attorney for service. File online through the relevant registry portal.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Ontario Declaration
Statement appointing local attorney for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an extra-provincial registrar queries the application, amend the information and resubmit. If a substantive conflict arises, obtain a legal opinion and, if necessary, file a court application for a declaration of authority to carry on business.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the business is digital publishing (NAICS 511210), which does not constitute an industrial establishment under Ontario's industrial facility licensing framework.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – no statutory operating license is required for publishing simulated social casino and virtual slots games; only a municipal business license and general IT-related permits apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (Ontario) – not applicable for this sector
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software publishing services are classified as non-toxic, zero-discharge operations and are not listed in O. Reg. 153/04 (Environmental Activity and Sector Registry).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or solid hazardous waste streams are generated. Office waste is handled by municipal recycling programs. Any server equipment must meet vendor energy efficiency specifications, but no environmental threshold is exceeded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain a municipal certificate of occupancy and pass fire safety inspection under the Ontario Fire Code. As a non-industrial premises, no structural load inspection is required. Workplace clearances under the Occupational Health and Safety Act require a first aid kit, fire extinguisher, and workplace safety poster.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) - national tax authority; online portals: My Business Account (MyBA) and Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CA LP is fiscally transparent for federal income tax purposes but constitutes a separate person registrable for GST/HST. To procure its statutory identifier, the LP, acting through its general partner or authorized Canadian agent, files Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Registration) or registers through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO). CRA issues a 15-digit Business Number (BN) plus an RT (GST/HST) program account. Non-resident partners must disclose their foreign TINs for FATCA/CRS reporting and Part XIII withholding matters. Where the LP is non-resident or controlled by non-residents, CRA may require GST/HST security under Excise Tax Act (Canada), s.241, and the LP must appoint a representative for service of documents and records access.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the LP is fiscally transparent for Canadian federal income tax (income computed under Income Tax Act (Canada), s.96 and allocated to partners; no entity-level tax), but it is a separate GST/HST registrant for taxable commercial activity. Non-resident partners of a Canadian LP carrying on business in Canada remain subject to Part I tax on their allocated Canadian-source income, subject to applicable treaty provisions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists under Canadian federal law; an LP is statutorily classified as a partnership. Available elections: (i) partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s.249.1; (ii) GST/HST Quick Method election under ETA s.227 (where eligibility criteria are met); (iii) annual GST/HST filing election under ETA s.238; (iv) designation of a partnership representative for GST/HST administration; (v) elections under ITA ss.216/217 available to non-resident partners with Canadian-source passive income, which do not extend to active social-casino publishing income; (vi) hybrid-mismatch deduction rules under ITA ss.18.2/18.3 operate as mandatory anti-avoidance limitations without an elective opt-out, though transparent-allocation alignments may be made in partnership filings.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under the Excise Tax Act (Canada); the federal GST rate applies at the CA_FED level, with provincial HST integration in participating provinces where the LP has a permanent establishment (e.g., 13% in Ontario).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies over the trailing four calendar quarters (small supplier threshold, ETA s.123(1)); new registrants are tested on a per-quarter basis at CAD 10,000. All app-based social-casino revenues via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing must be aggregated with other taxable supplies for threshold determination.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime for e-invoicing. The CRA voluntarily supports a Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework, but the LP remains obligated to file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or CRA-approved software, to preserve machine-readable books and records for at least six years, and to retain Apple IAP / Google Play billing statements, settlement reports, and commercial invoices. Invoices must disclose the BN, supplier identity, date, taxable amount, GST/HST charged, and explicit zero-rated designation for export supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of simulated-casino software, virtual slots content, and in-app digital tokens to non-residents of Canada qualify for 0% GST/HST under ETA Schedule VI Part V ss.7 and 10 where the recipient is a non-resident not registered under ETA and the supply is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The LP must substantiate non-resident recipient status, location of consumption, and the absence of Canadian-use nexus. Platform-mediated sales through Apple/Google require a true-supplier analysis: supplies characterized as made by the LP to the non-resident platform entity may be zero-rated, while supplies to Canadian consumers through the Canadian app-store channel remain taxable at the applicable GST/HST rate unless the marketplace operator is the deemed supplier.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) - applicable to physical goods only; inapplicable to digital intangible exports
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill - applicable to physical goods only; inapplicable to digital intangible exports
Inward Remittance Certificate / banking settlement statement evidencing receipt of export consideration
Apple Developer Program agreement and Google Play Developer distribution agreement identifying the non-resident payment-rail recipient
App-store sales reports and IP-geolocation / store-country data evidencing non-resident end-user consumption
Commercial invoices and delivery records documenting the digital supply to the foreign counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits of zero-rated digital exports center on transfer pricing, marketplace recharacterization, and true-supplier attribution. Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating claims expose the LP to: (i) reassessment of net tax with clawback of associated input tax credits; (ii) extension of the normal four-year reassessment window where misrepresentation is established; (iii) penalties under ETA s.280 (6% of the tax amount, increased upon subsequent infractions) and false-statement penalties under ETA s.280.1; (iv) criminal prosecution under ETA s.327 and Criminal Code s.380 for intentional evasion; and (v) daily compounded interest at prescribed CRA rates. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; however, the 180-day benchmark is retained as an administrative documentation standard for linking export consideration to zero-rated sales, and unrepatriated or delayed receipts will attract heightened evidentiary scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central bank; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the federal banking regulator; Department of Finance Canada (Minister of Finance) as the residual authority. Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange administration agency; exchange controls were abolished in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is freely floating and fully convertible under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Canada maintains an open capital account with no exchange-control restrictions on current or capital transactions, including inbound capital contributions, outward profit repatriation, and foreign-currency borrowing by a Canadian Limited Partnership. Profit remittances to non-resident partners face no convertibility or permit hurdle; the fiscal overlay consists of Part I income tax on the non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source business income (reported via T5013) and, for distributions sourced from designated payments such as royalties or interest, Part XIII withholding at a 25% statutory rate typically reduced under an applicable tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Receipts from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may be retained in CAD or USD indefinitely at treasury discretion. For Canadian income tax reporting, all foreign-currency revenue must be converted into CAD at the Bank of Canada's daily published exchange rate under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High for supplementary disbursement rails only; an offshore digital EMI is not a permitted substitute for the primary Canadian bank account. Legal constraints: the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) requires every payment service provider performing services in or into Canada to be registered with the Bank of Canada or to hold recognized transitional status; offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) must satisfy RPAA registration or act through a registered PSP to settle CAD. The CA_LP itself, as a merchant receiving Apple/Google settlements, is not a PSP and requires no RPAA registration. Treasury policy: restrict EMI usage to low-value subcontractor disbursements and foreign payroll; route all IAP settlement and partner distributions exclusively through the Tier-1 domestic account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is feasible at RBC, TD, BMO, and Scotiabank for clean corporate structures, but the CA_LP profile — non-resident limited partners and a digital-gaming revenue model — automatically triggers Enhanced Due Diligence. Each Tier-1 bank requires a video-conference KYC interview with the General Partner and any individual owning 25% or more of the partnership; a physical signing ceremony at a Canadian branch is strongly recommended to avoid a 30-day account hold. Mandatory documentation includes the provincial LP registration, the notarized Limited Partnership Agreement, and a Certificate of Incumbency for each foreign partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-model misinterpretation: social casino / virtual slots flagged as real-money gambling or an unlicensed money-service business under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement evidencing IAP-based virtual chips; (ii) notarized declaration that virtual chips have no cash-out or real-prize redemption value; (iii) technical architecture whitepaper demonstrating the absence of real-money wagering; (iv) legal opinion from Canadian gaming counsel confirming that Criminal Code (Canada) gaming licensing provisions are inapplicable; (v) CRA business number and NAICS 511210 / ISIC 5820 classification letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership of the Limited Partnership with non-resident limited partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Registered provincial LP statement/declaration; (ii) executed Limited Partnership Agreement with the capital contribution schedule; (iii) up-to-date Register of Partners including legal name, residential/business address, ownership percentage, and passport copy for every 25%+ partner; (iv) Certificate of Status from the provincial registry; (v) NR301 tax-residency certificates and economic-substance documentation for each non-resident partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Micro-transaction intensity: high-frequency, small-ticket Apple/Google IAP receipts lacking conventional commercial invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) 6-month IAP settlement statements from Apple and Google payment cycles; (ii) per-transaction reconciliation ledger with receipt ID, storefront, timestamp, and amount; (iii) refund/chargeback ratio report evidencing below 1% thresholds; (iv) compliance evidence with Apple Guideline 3.1.1 and Google Play Payments policy for virtual currency; (v) agreed-upon-procedures report by a Canadian CPA on IAP traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injections from foreign partner jurisdictions with enhanced-risk profiles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Source-of-funds declaration supported by originating-bank reference; (ii) audited financial statements of the contributing partner; (iii) corporate organizational chart showing all intermediate entities; (iv) flow-of-funds diagram restricted to recognized correspondent banks; (v) treaty-residency certificates for each contributing partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: the foreign partner's bank transmits a SWIFT MT103 to the CA_LP's CAD operating account at the Tier-1 Canadian bank; field 70 (Remittance Information) must read 'LP Capital Contribution — [Partner Legal Name] — LP Agreement Article [X]'. Canada does not operate a centralized purpose-code system (unlike SAFE in China); classification is achieved through free-text remittance data and the bank's KYC profile. Compliance note: every cross-border electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more is reported by the receiving bank to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA; funds are not blocked, but hold risk arises if the remitter name on the MT103 does not match the registered Register of Partners. Contributions exceeding CAD 100,000 trigger Enhanced Due Diligence and a source-of-funds questionnaire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail for supplier fees, licensing royalties, and contractor disbursements. Inbound IAP revenue is settled by Apple's and Google's respective distribution entities via periodic wire cycles at roughly 30-day lags into the LP's USD or CAD merchant settlement account; a same-day bank sweep converts USD to CAD for operating liquidity. Domestic operating payments clear through Payments Canada's Lynx system (high-value, real-time CAD wires) and the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batch ACH disbursements. Cross-border USD movements clear via Fedwire through the Canadian bank's US subsidiary or correspondent. Commercial Letters of Credit are generally inapplicable to download-and-license digital goods; a standby LC may be used only for physical procurement contracts above CAD 250,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with 1-12 month tenors under the Canadian FX Master Agreement or ISDA 2002 with Credit Support Annex
Plain-vanilla European-style CAD/USD currency options for downside revenue protection
FX swaps (swap points) to manage USD/CAD settlement gaps between IAP receipts and CAD operating disbursements
Cross-currency swaps for intercompany funding from non-resident partners
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for CAD are not available in market practice because CAD is fully deliverable onshore; OSFI-supervised banks do not offer CAD NDFs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Income Information Return (T5013) and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If fiscal year ends December 31: file by the calendar day immediately following the deadline for a partnership return in the CRA fiscal calendar (generally March 31); for designated partnerships containing a corporation as a member, the deadline is the 5th month after fiscal year-end; electronic filing of T5013 slips extends to 6 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $25 per day for each T5013 slip, maximum CAD $100 per slip; additional penalties up to CAD $2,500 for large partnerships; gross negligence penalties of 50% of understated amounts; criminal prosecution risk for willful non-compliance; administrative strike-off proceedings may be triggered by provincial registries upon persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 year-end); instalments, if required, are due quarterly for partnerships with annual taxable supplies over CAD $3 million.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty equal to 5% of the unremitted balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; further penalty for repeat failures; removal from active registry if outstanding returns accrue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial Limited Partnership Annual Declaration or Return (in each province where the LP is extra-provincially registered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Companies/Registries office (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; Alberta Service Alberta; British Columbia Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Normally within 60 days of the LP's registration anniversary (Ontario) or by a fixed annual date set by the province (British Columbia); effectively varies by province; must also be filed in the home province of the LP.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of CAD $100–$300 per province; administrative dissolution/cancellation of extra-provincial registration after 2 years of default; loss of capacity to sue or defend in provincial courts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (for the corporate general partner of the LP, if applicable; the LP itself files T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the corporate general partner's fiscal year ends December 31: individual-owned CCPC has 6 months to file (June 30); non-CCPC has 2 months (February 28); instalments due quarterly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of balance plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty; administrative strike-off by Corporations Canada if default continues beyond 1 year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No federal statutory audit requirement for limited partnerships per se. However, if the sole general partner is a federal corporation, the corporation may be subject to CBCA audit requirements (usually if public or if demanded by shareholders). Partnerships with gross revenue exceeding CAD $20 million or with regulated gambling/social-casino activities may be required to undergo an independent audit under provincial gaming regulations, payment processor contractual obligations, or securities/AML filings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; otherwise Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), which is Canadian GAAP; optional adoption of IFRS for unlisted entities; social casino operators typically use US GAAP or IFRS if reporting to international licensors/payment rails.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Canadian limited partnerships must file an annual confirmation of partners' information with the appropriate provincial/territorial registry after any transfer of limited partnership units. Generally, all transfers of 25% or more ownership in the LP must be reported to the registry within 15 days, and an annual declaration of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) is required on the anniversary date, confirming names, citizenship, tax residency, and percentage of economic interest. A federal beneficial ownership register is not yet mandatory for LPs, but provincial transparency laws (e.g., British Columbia, Ontario) require annual filing of registrable individuals.
